symbols.def: The conditional probability of observed orbit \(o\) given latent schedule orbit \(h\) and the uniform assignment law on orbit \(n\); the joint coefficient fixes both the assignment orbit and the observed orbit, and division by \(C_n\) normalizes each \((h,n)\) row.

symbols.def: An invariant estimator indexed by assignment and observation orbits.

symbols.name: orbitrisk

symbols.def: The exact rational posterior-mean estimator generated cell by cell from \(\pi^{\mathrm U}\) and the corrected kernel \(K\); this formula is a complete coordinate specification because every \(a_{no}\) and \(c_{no}\) is a finite rational sum.

standard.name: Binary potential-outcome support restriction for finite-population randomization inference

assumptions.condition: The schedule satisfies \(D_a(Y)\le s\) for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).

novel.justification: The condition is a transparent sensitivity restriction on latent potential outcomes, analogous to varying an unobserved-confounding radius. Smaller values are substantively plausible for pairs formed from near-duplicate baseline profiles, but pretreatment records cannot verify both-arm discordance; conclusions are therefore reported across analyst-selected values of \(s\).

assumptions.condition: The conditional assignment law satisfies \(Q_{\mathrm{design}}(A\mid Y)=Q_{\mathrm{design}}(A)\).

definitions.name: Ex ante assignment-law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak Q_{J,s}=\{Q_{\mathrm{design}}\in\Delta(\{0,1\}^{2J}):Q_{\mathrm{design}}(A\mid Y)=Q_{\mathrm{design}}(A)\text{ and }Q_{\mathrm{design}}\text{ is chosen from }(J,s,\mathcal P_J)\text{ before outcomes are observed}\}\).

definitions.name: Pair-preserving group
definitions.construction: \(G_J=\mathfrak S_J\ltimes(\mathfrak S_2)^J\), acting by pair permutations and independent within-pair label swaps on schedules, assignments, and observations.

definitions.name: Feasible schedule-orbit class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal H_{J,s}=\{h=(h_t)_{t\in\mathcal T}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{\mathcal T}:\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}h_t=J,\ \sum_t h_t\mathbf 1\{t\text{ is discordant in arm }a\}\le s\text{ for each }a\in\{0,1\}\}\).

definitions.name: Observation-orbit class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal O_J=\{o=(o_v)_{v\in\mathcal V}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{\mathcal V}:\sum_{v\in\mathcal V}o_v=J\}\), where each local observed unit is recorded as \((A_{jr},Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{jr})\).

definitions.name: SATE of a latent pair-type histogram
Assignment-marked observation polynomial
definitions.construction: Fix the lexicographically ordered representative of each \(t\in\mathcal T\) and set \(F_h(x,z)=\prod_{t\in\mathcal T}(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}}x_{\nu(a)}z_{\omega(t,a)})^{h_t}\).

definitions.name: Pair-orbit observation kernel
definitions.construction: For every \(h\in\mathcal H_{J,s}\), \(n\in\mathcal N_J\), and \(o\in\mathcal O_J\), set \(K_{hno}=C_n^{-1}[x_{00}^{n_{00}}x_{11}^{n_{11}}x_{\mathrm m}^{n_{\mathrm m}}z^o]F_h(x,z)\). Thus incompatible joint margins have coefficient zero and \(\sum_{o\in\mathcal O_J}K_{hno}=1\).

definitions.name: Exact \(J=2,s=1\) rational separation certificate
definitions.construction: Order assignment orbits as \((0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,0),(1,1),(2,0)\) and set \(q^{\mathrm U}=(36,30,1,30,2,1)/100\). Order \(\mathcal H_{2,1}\) lexicographically as specified by \(\pi^{\mathrm U}\), use its displayed 38 rational coordinates, and set \(\eta^{\mathrm U}_{no}=c_{no}(\pi^{\mathrm U})/a_{no}(\pi^{\mathrm U})\) on positive-mass cells and zero otherwise. Use the displayed 38 rational coordinates of \(\pi^{\mathrm H}\) for the canonical-segment lower certificate.

definitions.name: Exact finite optimal-design correspondence
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal Q^*(J,s)=\{q\in\Delta(\mathcal N_J):\text{there exists }\eta\text{ with }\max_{h\in\mathcal H_{J,s}}\mathcal R_h(q,\eta)=R^*(J,s)\}\).

definitions.name: Normalized assignment-orbit law
definitions.construction: \(\mu_q=q\circ\{n\mapsto(n_{00}/J,n_{11}/J,n_{\mathrm m}/J)\}^{-1}\in\mathcal P(\Delta_2)\), where \(\mathcal P(\Delta_2)\) is equipped with the topology of weak convergence.

definitions.name: Second-order pair-orbit selection handle
definitions.construction: Derive a local asymptotic decision experiment from the ten-type schedule simplex and kernel \(K\), retaining the joint local fluctuations of \(\tau\), pair-type counts, and observation counts on every boundary face; then take the smaller-order variational risk on the tangent cone determined by \((s_J-J/2)\) and recover exact finite minimizers from its contact set.

definitions.name: Orbitwise composite-null \(p\)-value
definitions.construction: \(p_t(n,o)=\max_{h\in\mathcal H_{J,s}:\tau_h=t,\,K_{hno}>0}\sum_{n'\in\mathcal N_J}\sum_{o'\in\mathcal O_J}q_{n'}K_{hn'o'}\mathbf 1\{T_t(n',o')\ge T_t(n,o)\}\), with an empty maximum equal to zero.

statements.statement: Theorem 1. For every \(J\ge2\) and \(0\le s\le J\), averaging over \(G_J\) is lossless for the minimax problem. The full rectangular kernel has \(O(J^{20})\) rational entries of \(O(J)\) bit length and is exactly computable by coefficient recursion from \(F_h\). Moreover, \[R^*(J,s)=\min_{q,\eta}\max_{h\in\mathcal H_{J,s}}\sum_{n,o}q_nK_{hno}(\eta_{no}-\tau_h)^2=\max_{\pi\in\Delta(\mathcal H_{J,s})}\min_{n\in\mathcal N_J}B_n(\pi).\] An orbit law \(q\) belongs to \(\mathcal Q^*(J,s)\) if and only if there exist \(\eta\), \(\pi\), and \(v\) such that \(\mathcal R_h(q,\eta)\le v\) for every \(h\) and \(B_n(\pi)\ge v\) for every \(n\). This certificate decides membership of \(q^{\mathrm{pair}}\), \(q^{\mathrm{Ber}}\), and \(\mathcal C_J\), essential noncanonicality, and singleton uniqueness by coordinate optimization over the projected optimal face.
statements.justification: The full primal--dual contact system, rather than the value alone, is needed to distinguish canonical and correlated minimax designs.
statements.gap: Bai2023WhyRandomize gives the averaging move, SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 gives a scalar unrestricted game, and Kallus2021Optimality gives fixed-estimator mixed-strategy geometry; none gives this hard-budget all-estimator face.
statements.consumer: For each analyst-selected sensitivity value \(s\), a trial designer can enumerate the exact minimax assignment laws and select one satisfying operational support or balance constraints without losing minimaxity for \(\Theta_{J,s}\).

statements.statement: Proposition 2. If \(0\le s\le s'\le J\), then \(\Theta_{J,s}\subseteq\Theta_{J,s'}\) and \(R^*(J,s)\le R^*(J,s')\). At \(s=0\), \(R^*(J,0)=0\) and \(\mathcal Q^*(J,0)=\{q^{\mathrm{pair}}\}\). At \(s=J\), \(R^*(J,J)=r^{\mathrm U}_{2J}\), and \(q^{\mathrm{Ber}}\in\mathcal Q^*(J,J)\) with the nonlinear posterior-mean rule from the unrestricted binary experiment.
statements.justification: The endpoints are mandatory reductions: perfect pair agreement makes paired assignment exact, while a vacuous budget recovers the published unrestricted problem.
statements.gap: Bai2022MatchedPairs and Hull2026BoundedOutcomes motivate opposite endpoint prescriptions under different information classes; this proposition embeds both endpoints in one fixed-population model.
statements.consumer: Analysts obtain a monotone worst-case-risk sensitivity curve in \(s\), with familiar paired and Bernoulli procedures anchoring its two endpoints; the optimal face itself is recomputed at each sensitivity value.

statements.statement: Theorem 3. For \(J=2\) and \(s=1\), the rational certificate \((q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U},\pi^{\mathrm H})\) satisfies \(q^{\mathrm U}\notin\mathcal C_2\) and \[\max_{h\in\mathcal H_{2,1}}\mathcal R_h(q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U})<9065/100000.\] Its displayed dual prior satisfies \[\min\left\{B_{(0,0,2)}(\pi^{\mathrm H}),\sum_{n\in\mathcal N_2}q^{\mathrm{Ber}}_nB_n(\pi^{\mathrm H})\right\}>9102/100000,\] and therefore \(\inf_{q'\in\mathcal C_2,\,\eta'}\max_h\mathcal R_h(q',\eta')>0.09102\). Hence \(\mathcal Q^*(2,1)\cap\mathcal C_2=\varnothing\), with an all-estimator risk gap exceeding \(37/100000\).
statements.justification: A strict rational separation prevents the intermediate problem from collapsing to an endpoint switch or a paired--Bernoulli mixture.
statements.gap: Kallus2021Optimality shows mixed strategies can matter for fixed-estimator variance, but no published result gives a strict noncanonical separation after optimizing every measurable SATE estimator.
statements.consumer: For sensitivity analysis at \(J=2,s=1\), the result shows that restricting attention to mixtures of paired and independent assignment can be strictly suboptimal even after reoptimizing the estimator.

statements.statement: Theorem 4. For every budget sequence with \(s_J/J\to\rho\in[0,1]\), \[\lim_{J\to\infty}J R^*(J,s_J)=\min\{\rho,1/2\}.\] If \(0\le\rho<1/2\), then every sequence \(q_J\in\mathcal Q^*(J,s_J)\) satisfies \(\mu_{q_J}\Rightarrow\delta_{(0,0,1)}\), equivalently convergence holds in \(W_1\) on \(\Delta_2\).
statements.justification: The formula quantifies the exact robustness value of pairing and identifies the phase boundary where first-order risk stops selecting the design.
statements.gap: SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 and Hull2026BoundedOutcomes give the unrestricted endpoint constant, while Bai2022MatchedPairs gives a paired prescription under another criterion; no source derives this interpolation or concentration theorem.
statements.consumer: The curve maps an analyst-selected discordance fraction to the sharp first-order sample-size cost and identifies when the minimax design must concentrate asymptotically on mixed pairs.

statements.statement: Theorem 5. Suppose \(s_J/J\to\rho\ge1/2\). Let \((q_J,\eta_J)_{J\ge2}\) be any sequence of invariant procedures satisfying \(\max_{h\in\mathcal H_{J,s_J}}\mathcal R_h(q_J,\eta_J)=R^*(J,s_J)+o(J^{-1})\), and let \(\mu_{q_J}=q_J\circ\{n\mapsto(n_{00}/J,n_{11}/J,n_{\mathrm m}/J)\}^{-1}\). With \(\mathcal P(\Delta_2)\) endowed with the weak topology, every weak accumulation point \(\mu\) of the sequence \((\mu_{q_J})_{J\ge2}\) lies in \(\mathcal F_\rho\). Conversely, for every measure \(\mu\in\mathcal F_\rho\), there exists a sequence of invariant procedures \((q_J,\eta_J)_{J\ge2}\) such that \(\mu_{q_J}\Rightarrow\mu\) and \(\max_{h\in\mathcal H_{J,s_J}}\mathcal R_h(q_J,\eta_J)=R^*(J,s_J)+o(J^{-1})\).
statements.justification: This theorem identifies exactly why the leading minimax value cannot by itself determine limits of exact finite optimizers.
statements.gap: HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 gives covariance guarantees for one estimator and SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 separates first- and second-order risk in another model; neither characterizes this measure-valued first-order face.
statements.consumer: For each high-mismatch sensitivity sequence, the envelope identifies the macroscopic assignment mixtures that need an exact or smaller-order selection criterion.

statements.statement: Open-ended Question 6. Using the second-order pair-orbit selection handle, characterize \(\mathcal Q^*_{\infty}[(s_J)]\) exactly for every analyst-specified sensitivity sequence with \(s_J/J\to\rho\ge1/2\): give necessary and sufficient contact conditions inside \(\mathcal F_\rho\), prove recovery by exact finite minimizers rather than merely first-order-optimal designs, and determine how the answer changes with the local approach of \(s_J-J/2\) at \(\rho=1/2\).
statements.justification: Exact finite optimizers may select a strict subset of the flat first-order face, and that selection is the proposal's genuinely unresolved theorem-level content.
statements.gap: The Airy expansion of SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 selects a scalar unrestricted rule, but no published result handles a measure-valued design face, pair-type boundary experiments, or critical hard-budget sequences.
statements.consumer: The answer determines which first-order-equivalent laws are exact finite minimax choices at each high-mismatch sensitivity path and supplies a principled tie-breaker for design sensitivity analysis.

statements.statement: Proposition 7. For every analyst-selected \(s\), invariant law \(q\), orbit estimator \(\eta\), and \(Y\in\Theta_{J,s}\), the confidence set \(\mathcal C_{\alpha,s}(A,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\) satisfies \[\Pr_{A\sim q}\{\tau(Y)\in\mathcal C_{\alpha,s}(A,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\}\ge1-\alpha.\] The set and its interval hull are computable using the same \(O(J^{20})\)-entry rectangular rational orbit kernel as Theorem 1, including when \(q\) is correlated and essentially noncanonical. Varying \(s\) produces a coverage-guaranteed sensitivity family; neither its members nor their interval hulls are asserted to be nested when the design or statistic is reoptimized.
statements.justification: Exact coverage makes a nonstandard minimax law usable in small binary experiments without an asymptotic approximation.
statements.gap: Wilson2026MatchedBinary and Zhang2026FastBinaryCI rely on within-pair coin flips or product Bernoulli structure, while LiSpertusStark2025 handles stratification but not arbitrary correlated orbit laws on an optimal face.
statements.consumer: Investigators can report a finite-sample SATE confidence-set sensitivity family indexed by \(s\), with each member uniformly valid over its corresponding latent mismatch class.

sampling_model.design: For each analyst-selected \(s\), the assignment law is chosen from all outcome-independent probability distributions on \(\{0,1\}^{2J}\); after pair-preserving symmetrization it is represented by \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal N_J)\).
sampling_model.units: The \(2J\) labelled units and all binary potential outcomes are fixed; only the partition into \(J\) pairs is observed before assignment, while armwise discordance is latent.
sampling_model.treatment: A binary assignment \(A\) is the only source of randomness, and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{jr}=A_{jr}Y_{jr}(1)+(1-A_{jr})Y_{jr}(0)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No marginal positivity restriction is imposed; zero-mass assignment and observation cells are handled by closed quadratic perspectives and explicit primal completions.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no sampled nuisances. Nature chooses a fixed schedule in the sensitivity class \(\Theta_{J,s}\); risks, optimal procedures, and confidence sets are reported separately as \(s\) varies.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Given an assignment vector and an invariant estimator, uniform randomization over the permutation group is minimax under invariant states and a quasiconvex objective.
The mixed-strategy optimal design minimizes worst-case variance of difference in means over a structured conditional-mean class and may require randomization over several partitions.
For unrestricted binary potential outcomes, Bernoulli assignment with a nonlinear posterior-mean rule attains the all-procedure minimax risk, whose second-order term is governed by the Airy function.
Independent assignment remains minimax over all measurable estimators for unrestricted bounded potential outcomes, with an endpoint-supported least-favourable problem.
Within stratified designs treating half of every stratum, matched pairs formed by the prognostic index minimize the mean-squared error of difference in means.

For a fixed stratified experiment with unbiased and uncorrelated group-CATE estimators, homoscedastic outcomes, and group CATEs bounded by \(B\) outcome standard deviations, Theorem 2.1 derives the lowest worst-case-MSE estimator among linear combinations of those group estimators.
The Gram--Schmidt Walk design controls a covariance-based balance--robustness trade-off and yields MSE and asymptotic inference guarantees for Horvitz--Thompson estimation.
Under design unbiasedness for bounded finite-population totals, the minimax bound is attained if and only if inclusion indicators are pairwise independent.
Under within-pair coin flips, the worst compatible binary attributable-effect allocation is a single boundary corner and exact inversion needs logarithmically many binomial tails.
Exact binary ATE intervals under balanced Bernoulli or matched-pair assignment can be computed with \(O(\log n)\) randomization tests.
Exact conservative stratified binary ATE inference can be obtained by maximizing randomization \(p\)-values over compatible potential-outcome tables.

tldr: Known pairs are useful when their two units would respond similarly under each arm, but that two-arm similarity is latent. The integer \(s\) is therefore an analyst-specified sensitivity bound, and for every value the project jointly optimizes over all outcome-independent assignment laws and all measurable clipped SATE estimators. A pair-preserving symmetry reduction with a joint assignment--observation coefficient yields an exact finite conic game, an \(O(J^{20})\)-entry rectangular rational kernel, and a dual certificate for the entire invariant optimal-design correspondence; a rational \(J=2,s=1\) instance rules out every paired--Bernoulli mixture. The sensitivity frontier satisfies \(J R^*(J,s_J)\to\min\{\rho,1/2\}\), while at and above the threshold the leading term leaves a measure-valued face. The central open result is the exact smaller-order selection of limits of finite minimizers, including the critical approach to \(\rho=1/2\). The same corrected kernel gives a finite-sample confidence-set sensitivity family for correlated optimal laws.

project_justification.gap: Published minimax results justify paired assignment under prognostic superpopulation structure, independent assignment under unrestricted bounded schedules, or linear shrinkage under a fixed stratified design with observed groups and bounded group CATEs. They do not solve the intermediate fixed-population sensitivity class indexed by a latent armwise pair-discordance cap while jointly choosing the design and an arbitrary measurable estimator, and they do not distinguish first-order-optimal laws from limits of exact finite minimizers.
project_justification.niche: The sensitivity restriction breaks full unit exchangeability without treating unobserved potential-outcome discordance as pretreatment information. It leaves a finite but nontransitive observation experiment in which correlated assignment laws and nonlinear posterior-mean estimators can be jointly optimal.
project_justification.fill: For every selected \(s\), the project supplies the correctly normalized assignment-marked orbit game, a matching least-favourable-prior dual, exact canonicality and uniqueness certificates, a strict noncanonical separation, a monotone risk sensitivity frontier, a first-order measure face, the exact-minimizer selection problem, and exact randomization-test inversion.

related_work: Bai2023WhyRandomize establishes the group-averaging principle and identifies approximate invariance and joint design--estimator choice as a boundary; its theorem is used as a symmetry template rather than a target to beat. Kallus2021Optimality shows that structured minimax design can require a mixed strategy, but its precision criterion fixes difference in means. SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 and Hull2026BoundedOutcomes solve the unrestricted bounded all-estimator problem by symmetries that do not preserve separate armwise pair-discordance sensitivity classes; Proposition 2 recovers their binary endpoint. Bai2022MatchedPairs obtains matched-pair optimality inside stratified half-treatment designs under a superpopulation precision criterion, which informs the low-sensitivity endpoint but does not make both-arm discordance observable. deChaisemartin2022Shrinkage, Theorem 2.1, derives minimax-linear shrinkage of observed group-CATE estimators under a bound on group CATE magnitudes. Its formal problem fixes the stratified design and observed groups and optimizes only over linear estimators, whereas this project imposes latent armwise within-pair outcome discordance and jointly optimizes the assignment law and every measurable estimator; it therefore informs the bias--variance motivation but is not a theorem-level target. HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 controls a covariance-based balance--robustness frontier for Horvitz--Thompson estimation and informs the assignment-measure geometry. AronowLopatto2026 gives an independence frontier under design unbiasedness, while the present comparison permits biased nonlinear estimators. Wilson2026MatchedBinary, Zhang2026FastBinaryCI, and LiSpertusStark2025 inform exact inversion; their product or fixed-stratum mechanisms do not cover correlated noncanonical laws or an analyst-indexed latent mismatch class.
technical_internal_limitation: A corrected checker formed \(K_{hno}\) from the joint assignment-marked coefficient and verified \(\sum_oK_{hno}=1\) for every \((h,n)\) at all \(J=2,3,4\) and \(0\le s\le J\). The resulting schedule-orbit counts are \((10,38,55)\), \((20,96,184,220)\), and \((35,195,454,650,715)\); the largest full rectangular array has \(7{,}668{,}375\) entries at \(J=4,s=4\), consistent with \(O(J^{20})\). The recomputed minimax risks by increasing \(s\) are \((0,0.0904264890,0.1030826943)\) for \(J=2\), \((0,0.0584446250,0.0719156622,0.0756571245)\) for \(J=3\), and \((0,0.0414059556,0.0546757329,0.0591555795,0.0601329999)\) for \(J=4\). Projected second-order-cone coordinate optimization reproduces the all-mixed singleton at \(s=0\), broad faces at the unrestricted endpoints, and the strict noncanonical \(J=2,s=1\) instance; the critical grids \(J=2,s=1\) and \(J=4,s=2\) have materially different finite coordinate-range patterns. Because these finite critical cases do not establish a stable sequence law, Open-ended Question 6 remains at its stated resolution. Only the \(J=2,s=1\) separation is backed by exact rational inequalities; the other displayed risks and face diagnostics are numerical early-kill checks, not theorem contributions.
honest_scope: The parameter \(s\) is an analyst-selected sensitivity index for latent both-arm discordance, not a practitioner-known or administratively verifiable quantity. Every risk, optimal face, asymptotic regime, and confidence set is conditional on the selected value or sequence, so substantive reporting varies \(s\) rather than selecting it from observed outcomes. The corrected finite orbit representation, endpoint reductions, rational noncanonical separation, first-order value, low-sensitivity concentration, high-sensitivity first-order envelope, and exact inversion are theorem obligations. The complete limit set of exact finite minimizers for \(\rho\ge1/2\) is the principal open object. At \(s=0\) the problem reduces to exact paired recovery; at \(s=J\) it reduces to the unrestricted Bernoulli nonlinear minimax experiment of SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 and Hull2026BoundedOutcomes.

seed_details.kernel: Reduce the bounded pair-discordance problem without loss to a polynomial-size orbit experiment and characterize the projection of the entire optimal procedure face by matching primal and least-favourable-prior certificates.

novelty_justification: The closest all-estimator results are SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 and Hull2026BoundedOutcomes. They solve the unrestricted bounded schedule class because independent transformed-coordinate swaps make assignments transitive; those swaps do not preserve separate armwise pair-discordance budgets. Bai2023WhyRandomize supplies the group-averaging principle but fixes the estimator in its first theorem and explicitly leaves joint design--estimator choice under approximate invariance open. deChaisemartin2022Shrinkage studies a different formal decision problem: the stratified design and observed groups are fixed, group CATE magnitudes are bounded, and minimization is restricted to linear combinations of group estimators; here the discordance restriction concerns latent armwise within-pair outcomes and both the assignment law and every measurable estimator are optimized. The strict delta is therefore not another endpoint risk or shrinkage calculation: it is the exact optimizer correspondence for the intermediate hard-budget class, together with a nontrivial phase transition and the smaller-order selection of limits of exact finite minimizers. The full first-order face is deliberately separated from the open exact-minimizer face so the proposal does not pass off asymptotic near-optimality as exact selection.
